newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany non-committal on Romania NATO bid timing.
newsitem.headline: Germany non-committal on Romania NATO bid timing.

text.p: Germany supports Romania's bid to join NATO "soon" but won't take any firm position on whether the alliance should expand by three, four or five members until the Madrid summit, a senior government official said on Thursday.

The official said Chancellor Helmut Kohl fully supports Romania's desire for NATO membership, but said Kohl believes the decision on how many countries join the alliance should be made by all 16 NATO nations at the July 8-9 summit in Madrid.

"Chancellor Kohl is in favour of Romania's entry 'soon,'" said the official, speaking on the condition he not be named. "It would be a misinterpretation of his remarks to take 'soon' to mean at the NATO summit. There is no fixed date."
Romanian President Emil Constantinescu met Kohl in Bonn on Wednesday to elicit support from Germany, whose voice could be decisive in Madrid.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be invited to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation at the summit in a first wave of enlargement.

While the United States wants to limit the first enlargement to the three favourites, many European NATO members want Slovenia and Romania included. Germany has remained officially non-committal despite growing pressure from the two sides.

There was no news briefing after Kohl and Constantinescu met, but Kohl's spokesman issued a statement saying the chancellor and German government had "a lot of sympathy for the Romanian desire for early NATO membership and supports it."

The acting head of the Romanian embassy in Bonn said there was no doubt Kohl supported Romania's bid, but said there was in essence no change in Germany's non-committal stance on whether Romania and Slovenia should be added to the enlargement.
